correctness.rationale: For any odd prime power \(q\) and \(n\ge1\), group inversion gives the central shift \(z-c-\ell_{a,b}(x,y)\) with a nonzero horizontal functional for every noncentral translation. Finite-character orthogonality forces all horizontal modulations outside the annihilator to vanish. Substituting \(w=z-c-h\) factors the remaining coefficient as \(\psi(\lambda c)\widehat U(W+\lambda)\overline{\widehat U(\lambda)}/(qE)\); central translations yield \(A_U(c,W)/E\). These identities prove the support formula \((N-q)r^2+a\) for every nonzero complex central profile. For a quadratic chirp, a one-dimensional Gauss sum gives \(|\widehat U|=\sqrt q\); its ambiguity function is supported precisely where \(W=2\alpha c\). This yields the two exact magnitude tiers, moments and Shannon entropy. The supplied checker verifies complete prime-field STFTs in five exact cyclotomic configurations and independently verifies the arbitrary-profile factorization for \(q=3,5\); finite checks supplement rather than replace the general proof.

value.rationale: The full-profile theorem reduces an otherwise \(N^2\)-sized noncommutative time-frequency support problem to the natural one-dimensional Fourier and ambiguity supports \(r\) and \(a\). The quadratic consequence determines a complete two-level law and exact entropy excess relative to an abelian coordinate group of equal size, providing a reusable extremal benchmark motivated directly by recent Heisenberg entropy-uncertainty literature. It is not an arbitrary finite census or an unmotivated parameter cutoff; no claim to a global optimal inequality is made.
